title: Insertion tabs: Floor ticket
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
The archive needs insertion tabs for new labels without disturbing an existing sorted drawer. Mina is checking the lower stop before the ribbon press opens. A negative reading is a real measurement and must not be replaced by an invented zero.

The input contains two rows: a sorted drawer and query values. For each query, produce the first index whose drawer value is at least that query; use the drawer's length if no such index exists.

Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement insertionTabsFloorTicket(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(q log(n+1)); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
